sources.entry: Flyimg - Resize and crop images on the fly. Get optimised images with MozJPEG, WebP or PNG using ImageMagick, with an efficient caching system. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: Flyimg is a Dockerized, self-hosted image service that resizes, crops, and compresses images on the fly from URL parameters, caching the results.
summary.what_it_does: Fetches a source image (from a URL or a path on the server), applies options passed in the URL such as width, height, crop and quality, and serves the converted result. Output formats include AVIF (default when the browser supports it), WebP, MozJPEG-compressed JPEG, PNG and GIF, with JPEG XL available via ImageMagick when enabled. The o_auto option negotiates the output format from the request's Accept header. Generated images are stored and served from cache on later requests. The project is run as a single Docker container with nginx and php-fpm.
use_cases: resize images on the fly via URL
convert images to WebP or AVIF
crop and compress product or thumbnail images
cache transformed images for faster delivery
notable: Generates AVIF by default when the browser supports it, with WebP, MozJPEG, PNG and GIF output
Optional JPEG XL output with o_jxl and jxlef effort tuning
o_auto format negotiation based on the Accept header
Single Docker container acts as a Cloudinary-like image service
Configurable via a parameters.yml file mounted into the container
caveats: Development build requires running composer install inside the container and can take several minutes
A managed SaaS version is offered as a paid alternative to self-hosting
README notes the JPEG XL output requires enabling it in ImageMagick
